title: SA20 Season 5: Marsh, Root Lead Star-Studded Signings as Du Plessis Era Ends at JSK
excerpt: The South African T20 league reveals its strongest-ever player pool with Durban assembling a superteam, while Joburg Super Kings release 14 players including long-serving captain Faf du Plessis.
body:
• Australia's Mitchell Marsh, England's Joe Root, Sam Curran, and Phil Salt headline the marquee pre-signings for SA20 Season 5, set to take place in January-February 2027.
  • Former JSK captain Faf du Plessis has been released along with 13 other players including Imran Tahir, Reece Topley, and Trent Boult, marking a significant squad overhaul across franchises.
  • Durban's Super Giants emerge as the strongest squad on paper with 19 players retained including Heinrich Klaasen, Jos Buttler, Aiden Markram, Sunil Narine, and Kane Williamson.
  • The player auction is scheduled for 7 October 2026 in Johannesburg, with several prominent overseas slots still to be filled.

South Africa's premier T20 franchise league has unveiled its Season 5 squad compositions, with a string of marquee international signings headlined by Australia all-rounder Mitchell Marsh and England batting stalwart Joe Root. The reveals also brought a notable departure: veteran South African Faf du Plessis, who captained the Joburg Super Kings since the league's inception, has been released.

The Marquee Additions

The pre-signing window produced a star-studded cast of international arrivals. Mitchell Marsh joins the Sunrisers Eastern Cape alongside Bangladesh spinner Rishad Hossain. Joe Root, who was already signed as an overseas player at the Paarl Royals last season, returns as the franchise's wildcard pick. Sam Curran heads to Durban's Super Giants, while England wicketkeeper-batter Phil Salt signs with the Pretoria Capitals alongside Australia's Matthew Short.

MI Cape Town have secured Will Jacks from the Pretoria Capitals in a notable pre-signing, adding the explosive England all-rounder to a squad already featuring Rashid Khan and Kagiso Rabada. Jason Holder brings experience to the Joburg Super Kings as they rebuild following du Plessis's departure.

Du Plessis and the Great Exodus

The most significant storyline is the sweeping squad overhaul across franchises. Joburg Super Kings released 14 players, the largest cull of any team. Du Plessis, 41, led the side through all four seasons of the tournament and was instrumental in establishing the franchise's identity. His release, alongside long-serving spinner Imran Tahir, signals a decisive shift toward a younger roster.

Other notable departures include New Zealand pace bowler Trent Boult from MI Cape Town, West Indian stalwart Kieron Pollard, Afghanistan spinner Noor Ahmad from Durban's Super Giants, and England pair Will Jacks and Shai Hope from the Pretoria Capitals — though Jacks has been snapped up by MI Cape Town.

The Power Rankings

Durban's Super Giants look formidable on paper, having retained all 19 squad places. Their roster reads like a T20 all-star team: Heinrich Klaasen (wildcard), Jos Buttler, Aiden Markram, Kane Williamson, Liam Livingstone, Sunil Narine, Kwena Maphaka, Gerald Coetzee, and Tony de Zorzi — complemented by the pre-signing of Sam Curran.

Sunrisers Eastern Cape retained 15 players including Tristan Stubbs, Marco Jansen (wildcard), Quinton de Kock, Anrich Nortje, and Jonny Bairstow, with Marsh and Hossain added as pre-signings. The Paarl Royals have locked in David Miller, Lhuan-dre Pretorius, and Joe Root.

The Auction and What's Next

The player auction is scheduled for 7 October 2026 in Johannesburg. Pretoria Capitals, having retained only Andre Russell as a wildcard and Will Jacks and Sherfane Rutherford as pre-signings, have the largest purse to work with and the most aggressive rebuilding to do.

For cricket-mad Indian diaspora fans, the SA20's growing investment in international talent mirrors the IPL's franchise model. The league's January-February window offers competitive cricket during the Indian off-season, and the presence of Indian-connected players like Rashid Khan, Sunil Narine, and the highly-rated Kwena Maphaka makes the tournament increasingly relevant for subcontinental audiences.
